chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from ʿAli ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Ibn Muskan, from Abi Khalid, from Abi ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I was with Dawud ibn ʿAli when a man who had killed another man was brought to him. Dawud ibn ʿAli said to him, “What do you say? Did you kill this man?” He said, “Yes, I killed him.” He said, “Dawud then said to him, ‘And why did you kill him?’” He said, “He replied: He used to enter upon me in my house without my permission, so I sought help against him from the governors who were before you, and they instructed me that if he entered without my permission, I should kill him. So I killed him.”

He said: Dawud then turned to me and said, “O Aba ʿAbdillah, what do you say regarding this?” He said: I said to him, “I hold that he has confessed to killing a Muslim man, so execute him.” He said: So he ordered concerning him, and he was executed.

Then Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام said: “Some people from the companions of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله were gathered, and among them was Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah. They said, ‘O Saʿd, what would you say if you went to your house and found in it a man upon the belly of your wife—what would you do to him?’ He said: Saʿd replied, ‘By Allah, I would strike his neck with the sword.’ He said: Then the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله came out while they were in that conversation and said, ‘O Saʿd, who is this one about whom you said: I would strike his neck with the sword?’”

He said: “So he was informed of what they had said and what Saʿd had said.” He said: “Thereupon the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: ‘O Saʿd, then where are the four witnesses whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has mentioned?’” He said: “Saʿd said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, even after the sight of my own eyes and Allah’s knowledge concerning him that he has indeed done it?’” The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Yes, by Allah, O Saʿd—even after the sight of your own eyes and Allah’s knowledge that he has indeed done it. Allah, Exalted is He, has set for everything a limit, and has set a penalty upon whoever transgresses the limits of Allah, and He has made what is short of four witnesses concealed among the Muslims.”

key_terms.أَقَرَّ: confessed or admitted to the act before authority
key_terms.الشُّهُودُ الْأَرْبَعَةُ: the four witnesses required as legal proof in a zina accusation
key_terms.حَدًّا: a divinely fixed limit or prescribed legal punishment
key_terms.حُدُودَ اللَّهِ: the legal and moral boundaries set by Allah
key_terms.رَجُلٍ مُسْلِمٍ: a Muslim man whose blood is legally protected
key_terms.مَسْتُورًا: kept concealed and not exposed without the required legal proof

ai.seo_question: Can a person lawfully kill someone for entering his house or for being found with his wife without four witnesses?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes a legal ruling regarding unlawful killing and clarifies that personal observation alone does not justify carrying out punishment in matters requiring formal proof. It also cites a prophetic precedent showing that in accusations of zina, the requirement of four witnesses remains binding, and anything less than that is to remain concealed among the Muslims.
